items.title: Goldman Sachs identifies 42 Indian stocks riding AI build-out
items.description: Several Indian companies are emerging as significant players in the AI infrastructure sector, according to Goldman Sachs. These 'AI Enablers' span industries such as power, data centres, and semiconductors. While the Nifty index has fallen, this group of companies has experienced substantial gains. However, their valuations remain high, with a noted premium over MSCI India. This trend signals a changing investment landscape within the Indian market.

items.title: Stocks in news: Tata Group, ITC, IRFC, NCC, Zydus Lifesciences and JSW Energy
items.description: The Indian equity markets faced a significant downturn, with benchmark indices slipping past vital support thresholds. The Nifty 50 saw a decline of 360.25 points, reflecting increased investor anxiety. Key players like Tata Group, ITC, and Indian Railway Finance Corporation draw attention following recent news. Analysts suggest that if the market falls further below these critical levels, the correction may continue.

items.title: Pre-market action: Here's the trade setup for today's session
items.description: Indian benchmark indices opened the week with the Nifty index declining amid widespread selling pressures. Analysts indicate that a break below 22,700 could lead to intensified selling, potentially dragging the index towards 22,400. Meanwhile, the India VIX rose 12.1% to reflect increased market fear levels. Foreign portfolio investors net sold shares worth Rs 5,353 crore, while domestic institutional investors were net buyers at Rs 5189 crore.

items.title: Sebi clears Gautam, Vinod Adani of MPS norm violation
items.description: Securities and Exchange Board of India has cleared Gautam Adani and family of MPS violations accusations. While it imposed a penalty of ₹20 lakh each on two individuals for misinformation. The cases involve Adani Enterprises, Adani Power, Adani Ports and Special Economic Zone, and Adani Energy Solutions. Sebi found insufficient evidence linking the Adani family effectively controlling certain foreign investments.

items.title: Stock Radar: HDFC Bank stock breaks out from upper trendline of falling wedge formation; time to buy after nearly 30% fall?
items.description: HDFC Bank rebounded from its February 2024 support near Rs 680 and broke above a falling wedge pattern. Technical indicators, including RSI and MACD, suggest positive momentum, while experts see a potential Rs 770–830 target over 3–4 weeks.

items.title: NCC shares rally 5% after securing Rs 1,076 crore Andhra Pradesh drinking water project
items.description: NCC shares rose after the company received a Rs 1,076.71-crore order, excluding GST, from the Andhra Pradesh government’s Rural Water Supply and Sanitation Department. The order involves providing drinking water under a multi-village scheme on the Yeleru Reservoir for the Anakapalli segment in Andhra Pradesh.

items.title: Power Mech Projects shares gain 3% after securing Rs 279 crore order from Telangana Power Generation Corporation
items.description: Power Mech Projects secured a Rs 279.20 crore, three-year O&M contract from Telangana Power Generation Corporation for YTPS. The order covers ash and coal handling plants across five 800 MW units. The company reported Rs 3,113 crore FY27 YTD inflows and a Rs 17,317 crore order book, supporting sustained revenue visibility and growth.

items.title: Nifty indices rejig: Which stocks will see the biggest inflows and outflows?
items.description: The National Stock Exchange’s (NSE) semi-annual Nifty index rejig will take effect on September 30, with Nuvama Alternative & Quantitative Research identifying the stocks likely to see the biggest inflows and outflows.The brokerage expects BSE to attract the highest inflows of $594 million across passive indices, followed by Vedanta Aluminium, Adani Enterprises, Polycab and Power India. Wipro, IHCL, Reliance Industries, Shree Cement and United Spirits are expected to see the highest outflows.Here are the key additions and exclusions from major indices, along with the stocks expected to see the biggest flows.

items.title: Nomura initiates coverage on Allied Blenders with Buy rating, sees up to 20% upside
items.description: Nomura has initiated coverage on Allied Blenders & Distillers with a Buy rating and a target price of Rs 850, implying nearly 20% upside. The brokerage sees premiumisation, backward integration and margin expansion as key growth drivers, with EPS expected to grow at a 26% CAGR over FY26–FY29. Execution delays and slower premiumisation remain key risks.

items.title: 10 Nifty stocks that Motilal Oswal analysts are bullish on. How many do you own?
items.description: The Indian stock market has undergone a prolonged phase of consolidation since the bull run lost steam in September 2024, but Motilal Oswal Financial Services (MOFSL) now believes that cooler valuations, improving earnings, strong domestic liquidity and resilient economic fundamentals have strengthened the risk-reward for Indian equities. Here are 10 stocks the brokerage is bullish on.

items.title: Ellenbarrie Industrial Gases shares rise 5% after securing Rs 481 crore order from BHEL
items.description: Ellenbarrie Industrial Gases shares rallied 5.10% after the company secured a Rs 481-crore contract from BHEL to build a 1,200 TPD cryogenic Air Separation Unit for its Coal to Ammonium Nitrate Project. The turnkey project will be executed over eight quarters and is expected to be commissioned in FY29, expanding Ellenbarrie’s presence in India’s coal gasification ecosystem.

items.title: PB Fintech shares suffer Rs 37,000 crore shock in 4 days but Jefferies, Bernstein see up to 100% upside
items.description: PB Fintech shares have plunged 42% in four sessions, wiping out Rs 37,000 crore in market value after IRDAI proposed reforms targeting insurance distribution and dark patterns. While Jefferies cut its target to Rs 1,540, Bernstein retained an Outperform rating with a Rs 2,310 target, implying 100% upside.

items.title: Stocks to buy: JM Financial expects soft Q2 season for IT majors; check target prices for Infosys, TCS, others
items.description: The IT companies are all set to begin the Q2 season, with TCS kickstarting the cycle on October 8. JM Financial noted that investors expect some improvement in growth, given that Q2 is seasonally a stronger quarter. However, macro uncertainty and AI-led productivity continue, while competitive intensity has also increased, with the industry now entering the fourth year of subdued growth, it warned. Overall, the domestic brokerage expects another soft quarter for most large tiers. Here are its ratings and target prices for 6 major IT stocks under its coverage.

items.title: Vikram Solar shares rise 3% after securing 400 MW module order from leading EPC company
items.description: Vikram Solar shares rose 3% after securing a 400 MW module supply order for decentralised solar projects across Maharashtra. The company will supply 620 Wp N-Type TOPCon G12R modules from October 2026 through March 2027. The order strengthens its presence in agricultural-feeder solarisation and India’s expanding renewable energy infrastructure.

items.title: Tata Chemicals, Tata Motors PV, other Tata stocks slide up to 4% as Tata Sons rejig clouds listing prospects
items.description: Tata group stocks declined after Tata Trusts proposed restructuring Tata Sons to potentially remove its NBFC and CIC classification, which could allow the holding company to remain private and ease regulatory requirements linked to a listing.

items.title: Honasa Consumer shares fall 5% after Rs 643 crore block deal; Peak XV, Sequoia likely sellers
items.description: Honasa Consumer shares declined up to 5% after 1.4 crore shares worth Rs 643 crore changed hands in a block deal. The transaction comes after the Mamaearth parent reported a 116.5% YoY rise in Q1 FY27 profit to Rs 90 crore. The company has set a Rs 5,500-crore revenue target by FY31, aiming to expand EBITDA margins to 15%.

items.title: HBL Engineering among 3 stocks closing below VWAP
items.description: On September 29, three Nifty500 stocks closed more than 1.5% below their respective VWAPs, according to StockEdge’s technical scan data. VWAP represents the average price at which a stock traded during the day, weighted by trading volume. A closing price below VWAP indicates that the stock ended the session below its volume-weighted average traded price.

items.title: Bharti Airtel, Vi shares rise up to 2% after Aug mobile subscriber data. Which is Nomura’s top pick?
items.description: India added 55 lakh mobile subscribers in August, according to data from the Telecom Regulatory Authority of India. Reliance Jio continued to lead with 24 lakh new users, while Bharti Airtel gained 21 lakh and Vodafone Idea over 5 lakh. Jio holds a market share of 39.31%, followed by Airtel with 38.01%. The growth in urban subscriptions increased by 0.70% from July to August this year.

items.title: Auto stocks: Festive demand gets a low-base boost; can earnings justify valuations?
items.description: The Indian automobile market is witnessing robust retail sales as the festive season draws near. A significant year-on-year uptick of 81.8% was recorded in early September 2026, primarily attributed to a previously low base. However, analysts speculate that growth rates might decelerate in the latter half of FY27 due to last year's high benchmarks. Mahindra & Mahindra is anticipated to thrive, bolstered by an extensive product lineup.

items.title: Why is market falling today? Sensex slumps 700 points, Nifty below 22,600. 8 key factors rattling D-Street
items.description: Stock market Down Today: On Tuesday, the Indian stock market faced a substantial downturn. This sharp decline came after a previous drop exceeding 1.5% the day before. A staggering Rs 4 lakh crore was wiped off in market capitalisation, as investors reacted to rising oil prices and climbing bond yields.

items.title: Nifty SIP return fails to beat even bank FD over 5 years: Is this the warning sign investors can’t ignore?
items.description: New insights reveal that systematic investment plans in the Nifty50 have consistently underperformed, presenting a five-year XIRR of merely 4.5%. This result places Nifty50 below the returns of traditional fixed deposits. In contrast, midcap and smallcap indices have shown impressive gains. Analysts recommend a strategy focusing on individual stock selection and earnings growth rather than relying solely on index performance, prompting a reassessment of index-based investment approaches.
